summary: This video demonstrates how to use Quiver Quant and Alpaca paper trading with Claude to automate stock trades using MCP servers. It shows setup steps, placing orders, implementing a strategy, and backtesting performance, all without real money. The author encourages viewers to try the tools, noting that free accounts require manual updates of strategy holdings.

claims.text: Claude can place stock trades for you in a single prompt without manual work.
claims.evidence_quote: Claude can place trades for you in a single prompt, and you do not have to do any manual work.

claims.text: The video uses paper trading, so no real money is involved.
claims.evidence_quote: for the trades we place today, we will not be using any real money.

claims.text: AI will not have access to your actual bank account.
claims.evidence_quote: AI will not have access to your actual bank account, and no, it will not take all of the money out of your actual accounts.

claims.text: Alpaca paper trading account setup is quick and free.
claims.evidence_quote: setup is really quick, and it's also free.

claims.text: API keys act like passwords and should be kept private to prevent unauthorized trades.
claims.evidence_quote: API keys act a lot like a password, and so if anybody gets access to that password, they might be able to have access to your account and make trades on your behalf

claims.text: To set up the MCP server, you need the endpoint, key, and secret key.
claims.evidence_quote: we are going to need the endpoint, the key, and the secret key.

claims.text: The Alpaca app shows a disclaimer that paper trading uses no real money.
claims.evidence_quote: You are on paper trading, and no real money is being used.

claims.text: Claude may ask for permission before executing trades.
claims.evidence_quote: it might ask you for permission to actually execute the trades.

claims.text: The video demonstrates buying one share of Apple through Claude.
claims.evidence_quote: the next thing that we're gonna test out is purchasing one share of Apple.

claims.text: Claude successfully implemented the Quiver Congress buys strategy.
claims.evidence_quote: It was able to successfully put in all of the positions held by the Quiver Congress buys strategy.

claims.text: With a free account, you cannot schedule the algorithm to rebalance automatically.
claims.evidence_quote: you cannot set some sort of schedule for the algorithm to rerun and update your holdings.

claims.text: The backtest in the video used the Pelosi strategy and compared it to the market.
claims.evidence_quote: it looks like it grabbed up the Pelosi strategy, um, how that performed over time and how that performed in comparison to the market.
